# Xenomorphs
[color=#999999][italic]"Unidentified lifesigns detected coming aboard the station. Secure any exterior access, including ducting and ventilation."[/italic][/color]
Xenomorphs come in two kinds: - [bold]The hive[/bold]: [color=#a855f7]alien larvae[/color] played by people, who crawl out of the vents, grow, and turn the crew into hosts for more of them. - [bold]An infestation[/bold]: computer-controlled xenomorphs that pour out of the vents in one part of the station. They fight, but they do not breed (see the end of this page).
## The life cycle - A [bold]larva[/bold] dies at 25 damage and has no hands. It can hide under tables and clutter with [bold]Hide[/bold] and crawl through vents. It gains 1 growth every 2 seconds, or 2 on weeds or in plasma gas, which also heal it. At 200 growth (about 7 minutes, or half that on weeds) it picks a caste with one of its [bold]Evolve[/bold] actions. It cannot evolve while cuffed. - A [bold]drone[/bold] builds the hive. Only a drone can become the [bold]queen[/bold], for 500 plasma, and only while no other queen is alive, awake and played. - The [bold]queen[/bold] lays [bold]eggs[/bold]. An egg takes 3 to 5 minutes to grow. A grown egg opens when a possible host comes within 3 tiles, and 1.5 seconds later it releases a [bold]facehugger[/bold], which jumps straight onto a host within reach if there is one. - The facehugger knocks its host out for 50 seconds. If it is still on their face 10 to 15 seconds after it latched, it implants an [bold]embryo[/bold] and stays there, spent. - The embryo grows through five stages. It takes about 8 minutes on average, but the timing is random and can be far quicker or slower. The host's sneezing, coughing, sore throat and mucous come first, and aching muscles and stomach pain come later. At the last stage the host feels [italic]something tearing its way out of their stomach[/italic], takes heavy poison damage, and bursts within a few seconds. The host is gibbed. If a player was in the host, they become the new larva and join the hive. Otherwise a ghost can take the larva.
## Plasma and weeds Every grown xeno has a plasma vessel, shown as a counter on the HUD. Abilities spend plasma, and the vessel refills by 1 every 2 seconds. On [bold]weeds[/bold], or in plasma gas, a wounded xeno heals every damage type instead, three times faster lying down. An unhurt xeno on weeds refills plasma faster instead. Plasma reagent in the bloodstream also tops it up.
A [bold]purple sac[/bold] (weed node) spreads weeds up to 3 tiles around itself. Weeds grow onto any floor, but not into space or past anything airtight.
## The castes A human sprints at 4.5. Health is listed as critical / dead. - [bold]Drone[/bold]: 100 / 200 health, sprints at 5, holds 500 plasma. It can Plant Weeds (50), Secrete Resin wall, membrane, door, nest or blob (75 each), use Corrosive Acid (200), Neurotoxic Spit and Acid Spit (20 a spit), Transfer Plasma, and Evolve into a queen (500). - [bold]Hunter[/bold]: 150 / 250 health, sprints at 9, holds 150 plasma. It can Leap at someone up to 4 tiles away, which pins them for 6 seconds and starts dragging them. It also has Tackle, Gut, Psychic Whisper and Transfer Plasma. - [bold]Sentinel[/bold]: 200 / 300 health, sprints at 6, holds 250 plasma. It has Tackle, Corrosive Acid, both spits and Transfer Plasma. - [bold]Queen[/bold]: 250 / 350 health, sprints at only 2.7, holds 500 plasma, heals fast on weeds and has 25-damage claws. It can Lay Egg (75), use every drone ability except Evolve, and use Psychic Whisper.
Every grown caste: - Has claws that deal 20 slash. - Can [bold]Devour[/bold] someone it holds in a grab and [bold]Regurgitate[/bold] them later. - Sees living things through walls. - Crawls through vents with empty hands. - Speaks on the hivemind with [bold]:a[/bold]. Anyone else only hears hissing.
Xenos cannot use guns, slip, freeze or get shocked, and they do not need air. They can melt their own resin walls by touching them, and resin doors only open for them.
## Ability details - [bold]Grabs[/bold]: Gut and Devour need more than a plain drag. In combat mode, press pull again on the victim you are dragging to tighten it into a grab. A Leap only starts the drag. - [bold]Gut[/bold] deals 50 slash to the grabbed victim and gibs them if that kills them. - [bold]Devour[/bold] takes 3 seconds of standing still. The victim stays alive inside and cannot fight their way out. They come out when the xeno regurgitates, evolves or dies. - [bold]Tackle[/bold] works on someone right next to you. It stuns them for 2 to 6 seconds three times out of four. Otherwise it fails and stuns you for 4 to 8 seconds. - [bold]Spits[/bold] stay readied after you click the action, and they fire wherever you click, up to once a second. [bold]Neurotoxic Spit[/bold] does 5 caustic damage and drains a lot of stamina, so about five hits floor someone. [bold]Acid Spit[/bold] does 40 caustic damage. - [bold]Corrosive Acid[/bold] goes on an object or wall next to you, never a person or something being held. An object collapses after about a minute, and a wall after about two to three minutes. - [bold]Nests[/bold]: only a xeno can strap someone into a nest. The captive needs 2 minutes of struggling to get free.
## Vent crawling Alt-click an open vent or scrubber next to you ([bold]Crawl through vent[/bold]). After 4.5 seconds you are in the pipes. Your movement keys follow the ducts one segment at a time, through bends, manifolds and junctions. Crawl into another vent or scrubber, or push out of an open pipe end, to climb out. Welded vents are shut.
Inside the pipes you can see the pipework around you, but you breathe and feel the pipe's own gas, and hot pipe gas hurts. Anyone near the pipe you are in hears something scrabbling through the ducts. If the pipe you are in is cut or unanchored, you are thrown out where you are, and a xeno that dies in the pipes slides out too.
# Fighting back
## Stopping facehuggers - [bold]Seal your face.[/bold] A facehugger dies against hardsuit and space helmets (anything pressure-proof), bio and radiation hoods, bombsuit and fire helmets, a welding mask, a light riot helmet with the visor down, a SWAT gas mask, the captain's combat gas mask, or a welding gas mask worn up over the face. - Any other mask, ordinary gas masks included, just gets torn off. A mask that cannot be taken off makes the hugger bounce off and die. - A hugger hits for 5 blunt damage even when your helmet stops it. - Eggs only open for someone a hugger could actually take. A sealed helmet lets you walk right up to them. - Only organic crew species can carry an embryo. Huggers ignore borgs, IPCs, synths and animals. - [bold]Never pick up a live facehugger.[/bold] Reaching for one puts it straight onto your face. Walking over one does the same. - A facehugger dies to any damage at all: any hit, any bullet, any real heat. Shoot it or stamp on it with a weapon. - A thrown hugger cannot latch on when it lands. It lies stunned for 3 to 10 seconds instead. - [bold]Shoot eggs from more than 3 tiles away.[/bold] An egg breaks at 100 damage, and the hugger inside dies with it.
## Saving someone who was hugged - [bold]Pull it off at once.[/bold] Use the strip menu on the victim and remove the hugger from the mask slot. This takes about 10 seconds, and it implants 10 to 15 seconds after latching, so start the moment it lands. You cannot do it yourself, because you are knocked out. - A removed hugger goes dormant for 20 to 40 seconds, then becomes dangerous again. Drop it and kill it. - [bold]Nobody can see an embryo.[/bold] Treat anyone who was hugged as infected. A spent, limp facehugger on someone's face means it already implanted. - [bold]Cure it with chemistry.[/bold] Parasiticide is made from dylovene, iodine and ethanol, one part each. 10u or more in the patient cures the embryo at any stage, as long as it has not started bursting.
- [bold]Or cut it out.[/bold] Lay the patient down or buckle them to a bed, chair or roller bed. Hold a scalpel, knife or anything else that slices, right-click the patient and pick [bold]Explore chest cavity[/bold]. It takes 10 seconds, deals 15 slash damage, and is interrupted if either of you moves or gets hurt. You cannot do it on yourself. - [bold]Rescue nest captives.[/bold] Anyone who is not a xeno can unbuckle a captive from a nest instantly. A nest breaks at 100 damage. - [bold]Free the devoured.[/bold] Someone swallowed by a xeno is still alive. Kill the xeno and they spill out.
## Killing xenos - [bold]Use lasers and fire.[/bold] Xenos take [bold]double[/bold] heat damage and only [bold]half[/bold] damage from bullets, blades and blunt weapons. - [bold]Stun and cuff them.[/bold] They have stamina like anyone else, so disablers and stun batons put them down. Grown castes can be cuffed. A cuffed xeno cannot leap, tackle, evolve or vent-crawl. Larvae cannot be cuffed, but they die to 25 damage. - [bold]Do not trust the dark.[/bold] Every grown xeno sees living people through walls. - [bold]Keep them off weeds.[/bold] On weeds they heal fast, especially lying down. Plasma gas in the air heals them as well. - [bold]Weld the vents[/bold] to keep them out of the pipes, and cut or unwrench a pipe to throw out anyone crawling through it.
## Clearing a hive - [bold]Destroy the purple sacs first.[/bold] They spread the weeds. A weed tile breaks at 20 damage, so a hit or two clears it. - Resin walls take 200 damage, doors 150, membranes 120 and nests 100. Weeds, resin walls and membranes burn in fires above 300°C. - Burn or shoot eggs from range. A growing egg that is broken leaves nothing behind.
## Infestations
Central Command announces that [italic]"Bioscans indicate that Lizards have been breeding in"[/italic] some part of the station. Despite the wording, that means xenomorphs. One minute later, purple sacs sprout from every vent within 12 tiles of that spot, and computer-controlled xenomorphs climb out. The bigger the living crew, the more of them come. Welding the vents after the announcement does not stop them.
These xenomorphs do not lay eggs or carry huggers, do not heal on weeds and are not weak to fire. They pry open and smash through doors to reach you. - [bold]Warrior[/bold]: 450 health, slow, claws for 30 slash. - [bold]Drone[/bold]: 150 health, as fast as a sprinting human, claws for 20 slash. - [bold]Spitter[/bold]: 200 health, slow, spits neurotoxin from range. - [bold]Vanguard[/bold]: 600 health and slow. It stabs for 30 piercing and spits acid. It takes only half damage from bullets and lasers, so bring a lot of people.
